artists.biography:
A Flock of Seagulls (also known as Flock of Seagulls) are an English New Wave band originally formed in Liverpool by brothers Michael "Mike" Score (keyboards, vocals) and Alister "Ali" James Score (drums), with Francis Lee (Frank) Maudsley (bass), and Paul Reynolds (guitar).
The group had a string of international hit singles including "I Ran (So Far Away)", "Space Age Love Song," "Wishing (If I Had a Photograph of You)" and "The More You Live, the More You Love", and became notable in the 1980s for their MTV video for the song "I Ran (So Far Away)".

perplexity.description:
Released in 1982 on Jive Records (later reissued by BMG), A Flock of Seagulls is the debut studio album by the English new wave band A Flock of Seagulls. The album is a defining work of the early 1980s synthpop and new wave movements, blending electronic textures with rock sensibilities. Characterized by its futuristic themes, catchy melodies, and prominent use of synthesizers, the album features standout tracks such as "I Ran (So Far Away)" and "Space Age Love Song," both of which became international hits. The band’s sound is marked by atmospheric production, layered keyboards, and guitar work that draws from post-punk and new romantic influences.

A Flock of Seagulls established the band’s signature style and remains their most iconic release, setting the stage for their subsequent albums. It reached No. 10 on the US Billboard 200 and No. 32 on the UK Albums Chart, while topping the charts in Australia. The album was praised for its innovative fusion of electronic and rock elements, and its success helped cement A Flock of Seagulls as a key act in the new wave era. The instrumental track "D.N.A." notably won a Grammy for Best Rock Instrumental Performance in 1983, further highlighting the album’s impact and critical acclaim.
